title: Bounded-below sequential Hom continuity from constructible integral sheaves
statement: Let ℓ be prime, E a finite normed extension of ℚ_ℓ, and X a scheme with Noetherian underlying space. For the ordinary integral coefficients R of def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients, let M be a constructible R-module sheaf. Let D be a sequence of complexes indexed by AsSmall(ℕ), with colimit cocone c and one common cohomological lower bound for Q(D_n). Then M[0] satisfies the property of def-weil-pbc-hom-colimit-property for D⋙Q and Q(c): for every integer shift, the canonical filtered colimit of additive Hom groups into the shifted stages maps isomorphically to Hom into the shifted colimit. AsSmall(ℕ) is equivalent to the ordinary natural-number category.

proof.text: Apply the good-truncation comparison theorem to replace the common cohomological lower bound by one common termwise lower bound, and the supplied cocone by the canonical cocone of a strict-bounded diagram N.

Obtain the finite extension tower of the constructible integral sheaf, using arbitrary condensed coefficients rather than a field-specific piece predicate. Locally finitely presented integral sheaves have Hom continuity by their two-term locally finite free resolutions.

For each locally closed piece, the coefficient-generic costalk-model theorem identifies its Hom diagram and cocone with those for a locally finitely presented sheaf on the stratum, keeping a common strict lower bound. Its compatible diagram and vertex isomorphisms identify the canonical colimit comparisons. Transport across the piece isomorphism.

Induct on extensionProductIter. The base case is the preceding piece continuity; the successor case is distinguished extension closure of homColimitProperty. Evaluate at the tower containing M[0]. The good-truncation comparison transports back to the original supplied cocone in every shift.
